text:
maya: Quick sync — follow-up on the API-key scoping RFC. TL;DR: we want project-scoped keys as the default, keep org-scoped for infra/admin only. Need migration plan + compatibility story. Thoughts?

kiran: +1 on project-default. We should gate org-scoped issuance behind an approval workflow and KMS rotation.

alex: How do we handle cross-project jobs like org-ingest that legitimately need multiple project accesses?

maya: Two patterns here: 1) give a service-account with explicit grants to the target projects, or 2) use a broker/token-exchange that mints short-lived project tokens. I lean broker for least-privilege.

sam: Broker is fine but adds latency + ops. We already have an authn-svc token-exchange endpoint — can we reuse that instead of a new broker?

jules: If we go broker/exchange we need clear audit trails + TTLs. Also a compatibility shim for older clients that expect long-lived org keys.

kiran: Proposed phased rollout: 
1) Phase A: accept both key types, implement translation middleware in API gateway to mint project tokens from org keys for approved flows.
2) Phase B: new keys default to project-scoped, encourage migration (CLI + SDK warnings).
3) Phase C: deprecate org-scoped issuance (12mo window) and hard-disable after migration.

maya: Example pseudo for apigw translation so infra has a starting point:
```
# apigw translation pseudo
if request.headers.get('x-api-key-type') == 'org':
  project_token = authn_service.exchange(org_key, target_project)
  request.headers['x-project-token'] = project_token
```

alex: That looks reasonable. Important: cache exchange results keyed by (org_key, project) to avoid adding 30ms to every request.

sam: Cache config proposal: TTL 30s, LRU size 5k entries, invalidate on role change events.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy of authn-svc v2 scheduled for 2025-09-18T19:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

maya: We also need AB telemetry: measure error rates, denied counts, exchange latency, and percentage of org->project translations. I'll draft a rollout playbook with metrics and rollback criteria.

kiran: :thumbsup: ping me when draft's up, I'll add RBAC mapping heuristics and edge-case rules (service accounts vs user-bound tokens).

jules: Also add migration helpers for SDKs (auto-exchange when building clients) and a bulk migration CLI for infra owners.

maya: Cool. I'll put up the draft in the next 48h and tag everyone. Follow-ups: decide cache sizing, approval workflow owner, and audit retention window. Link (placeholder): https://redwood.internal/docs/authn-migrate
